header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~42 mins
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Myers (Redwood PSM); Liam O'Neill (CTO - EmberCloud), Sara Gomez (Head of ML), Rajiv Menon (Infra), Nina Park (Compliance).
summary: Redwood product walkthrough focused on Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a multi-tenant SaaS use case with strict data residency and SOC2 needs. Discussed per-route token and latency visibility, cost attribution, batching/kv cache optimizations, and next steps to run a 24h benchmark and share pricing and security docs.
topics: Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SAML/SSO
transcript:
00:00 Alex: ok everyone, welcome and thanks for joining from EmberCloud, i'm Alex Chen from Redwood, i'll kick off and hand over to Priya for the console demo in a bit
00:08 Liam: thanks, yeah we've got about 40 minutes, want to focus on cost and per-route visibility mostly, sara will also ask about model quality tradeoffs
00:15 Priya: great, i'll share my screen now, bear with me if the sharing is slow, um — alright, you should see the Redwood Console home, top-level KPIs, tokens, cost, and active routes
00:34 Priya: first thing is usage analytics, you can break down by route, by model, by environment, we show token consumption, request count, and cost per route so you can attribute dollars to features
00:50 Sara: quick q: how granular is the cost? like per-api-route or per-tenant?
00:55 Priya: both — per-route natively, and you can tag requests with a tenant id, we have a cost attribution pane that maps tags to cost buckets, so you can do per-tenant billing or internal chargebacks
01:12 Rajiv: is that tag extraction done at our proxy or does Redwood attach it? we run an envoy sidecar currently
01:19 Priya: you can pass metadata in headers, or we can pull from your proxy. envoy works fine. small note, header names have to be consistent — sometimes the transcription of header names in docs is off, it's the same in logs though
01:36 Alex: we often recommend passing a tenant header early in the request to enable prefix caching and correct attribution
01:44 Priya: moving on, here's the per-route dashboard for our sample app, you see P50/P95 latency, tokens per request distribution, and cost per 1k tokens converted into dollars on the right panel
02:03 Priya: the cost model factors in model variant (e.g., 8-bit quantized variant vs full fp16) and hardware pricing if you're on Dedicated, so the console will show realized unit cost based on where the request executed
02:21 Liam: so when we run in Hosted, that unit cost is Redwood's list price, but if we go Dedicated the console will show our committed cost after discounts?
02:29 Alex: yep, exact. Dedicated shows committed billing profile, we also add metrics for utilization so you can see if you're overprovisioned or underutilized
02:40 Sara: can we surface a per-feature cost to product managers? they want a simple chart not a raw CSV
02:46 Priya: absolutely — we have a per-route cost trend chart export and scheduled report emails, also you can pin routes to a dashboard for PMs
02:58 Priya: note on end-to-end: batching and KV cache have big influence. the console surfaces cache hit rates per model/prefix, so you can see when prefix caching is saving tokens and dollars
03:16 Rajiv: excuse me, what's KV cache again— is that the key value cache for context?
03:20 Priya: yes, it's the kv cache we use for autoregressive models to avoid re-computing earlier attention keys, helps with streaming sessions and long chats. sometimes transcripts spell it out weirdly like k-v, kay vee, etc
03:35 Alex: there was a question earlier about quantization — we show a quality vs cost scatter for model variants so you can see e.g., base-8bit gives 30% cost savings with a 2–3% regen delta on our evals
03:50 Sara: hmm want to see that with our prompt set — do you support attaching eval suites to routes?
03:56 Priya: yes, you can upload evaluation prompts and run regression comparisons, and we tie alerts if a new model rollout regresses beyond a threshold
04:10 Alex: now flipping to dashboards, here's per-route top tokens list, top prompt patterns, and the ability to group by endpoint parameter like 'search' or 'generate'
04:23 Priya: uh, small glitch in the sample data but you'll get the idea — the console lets you drill into a single request and replay the tokens and model variant used, that's handy for debugging cost spikes
04:38 Liam: about spikes, what about autoscaling and burst — if we go Dedicated can we get buffer capacity for sudden traffic? we've had spikes to 5x baseline
04:48 Alex: yes, Dedicated supports configurable burst capacity and autoscaler policies. the console shows projected tail latency under current capacity and a cost delta if you enable burst nodes
05:02 Rajiv: network side — for Private/VPC, can we keep all inference traffic inside our VPC and still surface the same console metrics? our security team will ask that
05:12 Alex: for Private deployments we install a private control plane, metrics are routed to your observability stack if you want, or we can tunnel aggregated telemetry to the Redwood Console. network diagrams in the security pack show options.
05:26 Nina: about compliance — SOC2, KMS, and audit logs, can you prove access to model logs and who queried what?
05:34 Priya: yes, we have audit logs at the token/request level, RBAC controls, SAML SSO, and KMS/HSM integrations for model keys and customer data. i'll drop the SOC2 packet link after the call
05:48 Nina: you mentioned KMS, is that bring-your-own-key? and is it per-tenant?
05:53 Priya: BYOK supported for Private and Dedicated via KMS/HSM, and yes you can scope keys per-tenant if you want strict separation
06:07 Liam: any caveats around latency when KMS signing is used? we've seen auth calls add 20–50ms in some flows
06:13 Alex: generally KMS is async for bulk model artifacts; for runtime token encryption we recommend local HSM wrapping and the console shows the added p50 overhead in the latency panel so you can measure it
06:27 Sara: back to cost — can you show a sample cost breakdown for three routes: search, summarize, and chat?
06:33 Priya: sure, here's an example, route "search" is 40% of tokens but because it uses a larger context window its cost is 55% of dollars; "chat" has higher request rate but small window so 25% of dollars; "summarize" is infrequent but long outputs so it's 20%
06:51 Priya: you can also look at token types — input vs output token split, since for billing output tokens matter differently depending on model and if you're using streaming we show incremental cost over time
07:05 Rajiv: curious about batching — if we batch small requests into larger batches do you see latency impact? our product is latency sensitive
07:12 Priya: yes batching is a trade-off, the console has a batching simulator — you can tune target batch size and max wait, it will simulate expected p50/p95 and cost impact based on your traffic profile
07:25 Alex: often customers set per-route policies: low-latency for search (no batching, smaller model), high-throughput for embeddings (bigger batch, quantized model)
07:36 Liam: if we do a canary model rollout, can console show canary metrics side-by-side?
07:41 Priya: yes, there's a rollout view with canary vs baseline, model variants, and automatic fallback triggered on latency or quality regressions
07:52 Sara: you said fallback — is that at router-level? what about cross-region fallback? our users are global
07:58 Alex: routing policies support latency-first and cost-first fallbacks, and cross-region fallback is supported; you'll see the fallback events in the tracer and in the console timeline
08:10 Priya: another note: cache warming matters, the console can show when a model variant is cold and the expected cost for that warmup period, helps planning for rollouts
08:22 Rajiv: any limitations on models? we run some custom Llama-derivs and internal fine-tunes
08:27 Priya: we support most open architectures; for private models we provide an onboarding checklist, model packaging guidelines, and a compatibility test that runs in the runtime in a sandbox
08:39 Liam: security team will ask for data residency, does console store raw prompts in the hosted offering?
08:47 Alex: by default we store logs for 30 days with redaction options; for Private/Dedicated you can choose log retention and whether raw prompts are kept, and you can encrypt or forward them to your SIEM
09:00 Nina: perfect — we'll need the retention SLA in writing
09:04 Alex: we'll include retention options in the security docs we send
09:10 Priya: demoing anomaly detection now, console flags cost anomalies and can create a Slack alert or webhook; here's an example spike last week from a bot loop
09:25 Sara: we've had bot loops, nice — can we threshold by token or by dollar amount?
09:29 Priya: both, and you can exclude specific routes from alerts if you expect spikes during batch backfills
09:36 Liam: what's the setup time for Dedicated vs Private?
09:40 Alex: Dedicated onboarding is typically 4–6 weeks for a first pool, Private (VPC/on-prem) is 8–12 weeks depending on network approvals and HSM procurements
09:50 Rajiv: curious about cost math — can you export a forecast for monthly spend given our qps and routes? we want to show finance
09:57 Priya: yes, console has a cost forecaster — you input traffic profile, model mix, and it projects spend under different configs (hosted list price, dedicated with committed units, private infra costs) and you can export CSV to feed finance models
10:13 Alex: also note Optimize recommendations: the console will suggest batching/quantization and which routes to pin to cheaper variants to hit your target cost per request
10:24 Sara: can Optimize also recommend rollout percentage for canaries to limit risk?
10:28 Priya: yes, it gives a recommended gradual ramp and expected cost vs quality curve
10:34 Jordan: quick admin question — how granular is RBAC for console? can we lock down which PMs see cost but not raw prompts?
10:41 Priya: role-based access is fine-grained — you can create roles that only see aggregated metrics or cost dashboards and block request-level details
10:50 Nina: will need audit trail for any admin role changes
10:53 Alex: those are logged in audit events and included in the compliance pack
11:00 Liam: ok logistics, what's the next step if we want to run a pilot?
11:05 Alex: typical next step is a 2–4 week pilot on a scoped set of routes, we run a perf benchmark with your traffic replay and show the console dashboards end-to-end
11:14 Priya: action for us is to run the 24h benchmark on dev traffic and share the console export and cost forecast, that'll give you real numbers to compare Hosted vs Dedicated
11:24 Liam: sounds good, we'll get the dev token and sample traffic to you by end of day tomorrow
11:28 Alex: perfect, we'll follow up with the pricing and security docs. any remaining questions?
11:34 Sara: small one — how do you handle tokenization differences between models? sometimes token counts differ a lot
11:39 Priya: we normalize token accounting per model tokenizer and show both raw token counts and normalized token units so the cost forecast is apples-to-apples
11:50 Liam: ok thanks, that was helpful. we'll review and schedule a follow-up next week to align on pilot scope
11:58 Alex: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned
12:00 [call ended]
